standard_prerequisites.name: An integral ring map satisfies going up, and a morphism satisfying going up between affine schemes is closed, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives closedness of an integral morphism and hence, with base change, universal closedness.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of the scheme theoretic image of the closed subscheme cut out by a relation as the closed subscheme defined by the kernel of the corresponding ring map, and the resulting surjectivity, cited from the same chapter and an example of the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the image of the locally closed piece and shows it surjects onto the closed subscheme defined by the kernel.

standard_prerequisites.name: The identification of a pullback in the displayed square as trivial, because one map sends the variable to an invertible element while the other sends it to zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the bottom left corner of the diagram empty, which forces the bottom middle to be empty by surjectivity.

core_obligations: First direction: an integral morphism is affine by definition and stays integral under base change, so it suffices to prove closedness, which follows from going up for integral ring maps and the closedness criterion for morphisms satisfying going up (proof lines 11064-11070).

Second direction, reduction: assume the morphism affine and universally closed, work with the corresponding ring map, and reduce to showing that every element of the source ring is integral over the base ring, i.e. that the kernel of the map sending the variable to that element contains a monic polynomial (proof lines 11072-11082).

Polynomial manipulation: for the kernel of the induced map on the ring obtained by making the element invertible, the coefficients of any element of that kernel satisfy linear relations; these produce, for large indices, elements of the original kernel obtained by reversing coefficients, and if the constant term of the original element is one, the produced polynomial is monic (proof lines 11083-11096).

Reduction to emptiness: hence it remains to show that the kernel of the induced map contains a polynomial with constant term one, which is done by proving that the closed subscheme cut out by the kernel and the variable is empty (proof lines 11096-11098).

Emptiness via the diagram: universal closedness of the morphism makes its base change to the polynomial ring closed, so the image of the closed piece is the closed subscheme defined by the kernel and the map onto it is surjective; in the displayed pullback square the bottom left corner is empty because it is the spectrum of a tensor product in which the variable becomes simultaneously invertible and zero, so surjectivity forces the bottom middle to be empty (proof lines 11099-11118).
proof_roadmap: Use going up for the first direction, and for the second reduce to the statement that a certain kernel contains a monic polynomial, which is rewritten as the emptiness of a closed subscheme cut out by that kernel and the variable (proof lines 11064-11098).

Prove that emptiness by base changing the universally closed morphism to a polynomial ring, identifying the image of a closed piece with the relevant closed subscheme, and using the triviality of one corner of a pullback square to contradict surjectivity (proof lines 11099-11118).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a morphism of schemes is integral exactly when it is affine and universally closed (statement lines 11053-11064). The counted proof has real content in the second direction: after reducing to a ring map it rewrites the claim as the existence of a monic polynomial in a kernel, manipulates coefficients to reduce this to a statement about a kernel containing a polynomial with constant term one, and then proves that statement by base changing the universally closed morphism to a polynomial ring, identifying the image of a closed piece with a closed subscheme defined by the kernel, and contradicting the resulting surjectivity using a pullback square one of whose corners is empty (proof lines 11072-11118). It is H2: the reduction, the coefficient computation and the diagram argument are all carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard going up and scheme theoretic image statements.
